meta.titre: Matching sentence halves logically: purpose, condition, reason

sections.contenu_markdown: Matching sentence halves is a logic exercise as much as a grammar one: the right ending must make complete real-world sense with its beginning.

sections.titre: Types of connecting clauses in matching exercises
sections.contenu_markdown: A sentence beginning describing an action can logically combine with: a purpose clause ('to + verb' or 'in order to + verb', explaining why), a condition ('unless' meaning 'if not'), or a reason ('because'). Read each option and test which produces a sentence that is both grammatically correct and logically coherent.

sections.enonce_markdown: Match: 'Bintu went to the forest...' with the correct ending.

etapes.resultat_markdown: Only 'to find fuel wood...' makes sense as purpose

etapes.justification: 'to + infinitive' after a motion verb expresses purpose.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Bintu went to the forest to find fuel wood for her kitchen

sections.conclusion_markdown: The correct match combines both grammatical form and logical meaning.

items.erreur_markdown: Matching based only on grammatical plausibility without checking real-world logic.
items.pourquoi_faux: Several endings might be grammatically attachable to a beginning, but only one makes genuine sense in context.
items.correction_markdown: Always read the complete combined sentence and ask whether it makes real-world sense, not just grammatical sense.

items.enonce_markdown: Match: 'She saved money...' with 'to buy a new car'.
items.solution_markdown: She saved money to buy a new car (purpose clause).

items_markdown: Purpose clauses use 'to' or 'in order to' + base verb
Always test the FULL combined sentence for logical coherence
